Ivy: Quick UX flag — compact playground on small widths: when streaming is active the token counter briefly expands (digits shift) and the Stop/Regenerate chips get hidden behind quick-actions. Also, selecting a prompt from the library sometimes restarts the stream. Short gif attached.
Noah: can you drop the gif? want to see repro steps.
Ivy: https://files.internal/s/compact-stream-clip.gif
Shows chip disappearing after prompt insert during streaming.
Zara: Observed this too. Two problems: (1) token counter layout thrash when numbers change width; (2) prompt insertion triggers composer rehydrate which tears down websocket stream.
Omar: quick wins: use monospace for counter + min-width reserve (e.g., 5ch) to avoid shifts, and throttle visual updates to ~120ms. That reduces reflow.
Priya: Accessibility: icon-only stop/regenerate must have aria-labels ("Stop generation", "Regenerate response"). Floating stop should be keyboard reachable and have a visible focus ring. For streaming text use aria-live="polite"; add a "Read latest" control to assertively announce last chunk on demand.
Noah: For prompt lib, instead of full render we should patch the textarea value via insertText API so we keep the session id and don't re-request generation. If rehydrate is unavoidable snapshot the session token and resume without a fresh request.
Omar: CSS example for counter: ```css
.token-counter { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; min-width: 5ch; text-align: right; }
```
Zara: UX decision: floating circular stop (44px) pinned top-right of message frame vs collapsing quick-actions. I vote floating stop for discoverability; hide when not streaming.
Ivy: Plan: 1) Omar adds monospace+min-width + UI throttle (120ms), 2) Noah implements insertText + keep-session flow, 3) Priya writes a11y acceptance criteria and verifies focus order, 4) Zara mocks floating stop variants (light/dark/high-contrast). qa-bot: preview build will include mobile emulation.
qa-bot: Preview: https://playground.internal/preview/230450 (includes keyboard + contrast checks).
Ivy: Pairing: Zara+Priya on visuals at 14:30, Omar+Noah on continuity at 15:00. I'll track the follow-ups on the design board. Thanks!
